items.title: Performance of Large Language Models in Answering Juvenile Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Questions: A Blinded Expert-based Comparative Study
items.abstract: Background: Large language models are increasingly used to obtain medical information, but their performance in juvenile systemic lupus erythematosus remains insufficiently characterized. Objective: To compare expert-rated response quality and clinical relevance across 4 artificial intelligence (AI) models using standardized juvenile systemic lupus erythematosus–related questions. Design: Cross-sectional expert-based comparative study. Setting: Freely accessible consumer-facing web interfaces evaluated on December 30, 2025. Participants: Ten pediatric rheumatology experts. Intervention: Not applicable. Main Outcome Measures: Twenty standardized questions generated 80 AI responses, rated on a 5-point Likert Scale. Model performance was compared using the Friedman test with Kendall W and Bonferroni-corrected post hoc analyses; interrater agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Results: DeepSeek achieved the highest median rating [5 (1 to 5)], followed by Gemini [4 (2 to 5)], ChatGPT [4 (3 to 5)], and Copilot [4 (3 to 5)]. Overall expert-rated performance differed significantly among models [Friedman χ 2 (3) = 63.553, p < 0.001; Kendall W = 0.106]. DeepSeek outperformed ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot (all p < 0.001), while Gemini performed better than ChatGPT ( p = 0.007) and Copilot ( p < 0.001). Interrater agreement was highest for DeepSeek (ICC =0 .734) and lowest for Copilot (ICC = 0.043). Trust scores remained unchanged before and after evaluation [4 (3 to 5) vs. 4 (3 to 5), p =0.414]. Limitation: Single-time-point, single-response testing did not assess within-model reproducibility, and the question set was not formally validated. Conclusion: AI models differed in expert-rated performance and interrater agreement; outputs should be interpreted cautiously and with specialist oversight.

items.title: Phage Therapy and Phage-Derived Lytic Proteins in the One Health Era: Mechanisms, Challenges and Emerging Innovations
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a critical global health threat, as conventional antibiotics are increasingly ineffective against multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, particularly ESKAPE organisms. In response, bacteriophages and their derived lytic proteins, including endolysins, holins, and spanins, have emerged as promising therapeutic alternatives. This review examines the current landscape and future prospects of phage-based therapeutics within a One Health framework spanning human, veterinary, and environmental applications. We explore phage biology, including both lytic and lysogenic cycles, as a mechanistic foundation for understanding their role in addressing the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance. Additionally, we detail bacterial defence mechanisms, such as restriction modification systems, CRISPR-Cas systems, and spontaneous mutations that confer phage resistance. Lytic proteins demonstrate efficacy in treating systemic infections, disrupting biofilm, and targeting resistant pathogens across humans, livestock, and aquaculture. Although phage therapy is a promising antibacterial alternative, it still faces several constraints, including a narrow host range, immune clearance, complex pharmacokinetics, and the inability of exogenous lytic proteins to cross the outer membranes of Gram-negative bacteria. This review highlights emerging solutions to these challenges, including the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for phage and lysin discovery, machine learning models for predicting effective phage combinations, and the engineering of phage lytic proteins to broaden antimicrobial spectra. It also discusses combination strategies that pair whole phages with their derived proteins to exploit synergistic killing and counter the emergence of resistance, as well as advanced delivery systems designed to protect phage integrity and enhance activity in hostile physiological environments.

items.title: Phenomenologically Grounded Design of IoHT Spaces: Socioenactive Knowledge Creation Through Socially Aware Design
items.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) increasingly shapes human environments, yet a systematic review found few studies positioning people as constitutive participants rather than peripheral users. This paper introduces the Internet of Human Things (IoHT), a phenomenologically grounded framework centering humans in socioenactive spaces where social, physical, and digital dimensions couple continuously. Using the Socially Aware Design (SAwD) methodology and Engelland’s categories of World, Flesh, and Truth, we conducted four participatory design workshops in a hospital (2018; 14 children aged 7–11) and a school for neurodivergent students (2023), bridged by a pandemic-era remote phase. The resulting object taxonomy, organized along data-direction, manipulability, and infrastructure-role dimensions, serves as a situated design instrument. The socioenactive cycle enacts all four modes of Nonaka and Takeuchi’s SECI model, extending knowledge-creation theory into embodied, technology-mediated experience. IoHT contributes a phenomenological vocabulary and a design process for socioenactive knowledge creation in human-centered IoT environments.

items.title: Physics-Causality-Anchored Verification Theory (PCAVT) · 唯物实践论
items.abstract: Physics-Causality-Anchored Verification Theory (PCAVT) — formerly 唯物实践论 (Material-Praxis Theory) — is a formally constrained category-derivation system that takes carrying natural language (Chinese) as its symbol basis. It treats the Chinese sign system as a set of B1 constants and derives strictly, giving it a mathematical character: non-ambiguous, derivable, and self-consistent. Core outputs include the Three Laws (structural conditions for any shared symbolic system), the A-B-C six-subset framework (A material substrate, B information, C agent), and difference analysis (A2 − A1, the material net output of human practice). The repository publishes the methodology (5th edition), the self-reference-consistency statement, the formalization-alienation critique, and applied papers (economics, gender narrative, education, AI/LLM training-data quality), together with reproducible scripts and figures. This record archives the public repository as a citable research corpus.

items.title: Physics-grounded multi-agent architecture for traceable, risk-aware human–AI decision support in manufacturing
items.abstract: High-precision CNC machining of free-form aerospace components requires bounded compensations informed by inspection, simulation, and process knowledge. Off-the-shelf large language model (LLM) assistants can generate text, but they do not reliably execute risk-constrained multi-step numerical workflows or provide auditable provenance for high-stakes decisions. We present multi-agent knowledge analysis (MAKA), a decision-support architecture that separates intent routing, tools-only quantitative analysis, knowledge graph retrieval, and critic-based verification that enforces physical plausibility, safety bounds, and provenance completeness before recommendations are surfaced for human approval. MAKA is instantiated on a Ti-6Al-4V rotor blade machining testbed by fusing virtual-machining path-tracking error fields, cutting-force and deflection simulations, and scan-based 3D inspection deviation maps from 16 blades. The analysis decomposes deviation into an evidence-linked pathing component, a drift-based wear proxy capturing systematic evolution across parts, and a residual systematic compliance term. In a three-level tool-orchestration benchmark spanning single-step to three-or-more-step stateful sequences, MAKA increased the pass rate for correct tool selection, argument assignment, and dependency-consistent execution by a mean, median, and maximum of 22.9, 8.0, and 64.0 percentage points, respectively, across 15 model-level comparisons over the stronger of the ReAct-style and structured function-calling baselines with identical model and tool access. Digital twin what-if studies show MAKA can coordinate traceable compensation candidates that reduce predicted surface deviation from order 1 0 − 2 in to approximately ± 1 0 − 3 in over most of the blade within the simulation environment, providing a pre-deployment verification signal for risk-aware human decision-making.

items.title: Planning Concerts with AI: An Integrated Decision-Support Framework for Demand, Sustainability, and Economic Feasibility
items.abstract: Concert organizers must balance financial success, operational efficiency, and environmental sustainability, yet these factors are often evaluated separately. Artificial intelligence and workflow automation offer opportunities for integration, but integrated decision-support systems remain limited in concert planning. This study develops an AI-assisted concert-planning decision-support system implemented in n8n. It combines user-defined event parameters with external artist-popularity metrics and currency exchange services to estimate audience demand, environmental indicators, and financial feasibility, and generate structured planning recommendations within one workflow. A case study based on Coldplay’s Music of the Spheres World Tour concert at Olympiastadion Berlin demonstrates the framework’s functionality. The system predicted attendance of 72,306 spectators, approximately 97% of stated venue capacity, and generated planning estimates for energy consumption, carbon emissions, waste, transportation, ticket revenue, costs, and profitability. Because complete verified concert-specific data were unavailable, these outputs demonstrate system functionality and plausibility rather than validate predictive accuracy or reconstruct actual concert performance. The framework illustrates how integrated AI and workflow automation can support efficiency, transparency, and consistency in pre-event decision-making. It also shows how environmental sustainability and economic viability can be assessed together rather than as independent objectives. Intended to support early-stage feasibility assessment, the system does not replace detailed operational analyses or comprehensive life-cycle assessments. It provides a practical approach to more sustainable, transparent, and data-driven planning in the live event industry.

items.title: Platform Justice: Algorithmic Management, Worker Deactivation And Due Process In India's Gig Economy
items.abstract: Digital platforms have changed how work is organised in India. Ride-hailing, food delivery and home services give millions of people an income, yet most of these workers are called “partners”, not employees. Software assigns their tasks, sets incentives, tracks performance and can cut off their access to work, often without explanation. This paper examines algorithmic deactivation: the suspension, blocking or termination of a worker’s access to a platform through automated or partly automated systems. It argues that deactivation is not only a contractual matter. Where platform work is a main source of income, unexplained or arbitrary deactivation raises real questions of fairness, equality, privacy and access to justice. The paper reviews the Code on Social Security, 2020, Articles 14, 19 and 21 of the Constitution, the Rajasthan and Karnataka laws, and the ILO and EU approaches. It finds that India now recognises gig workers but does not yet regulate algorithmic management itself. It proposes a rights-based framework built on notice, reasons, human review, appeal, interim protection and independent oversight, while leaving platforms free to act against genuine misconduct.

items.title: Pose-Free Feed-Forward 3D Inpainting via Learnable Mask Attention and Support Token Refinement
items.abstract: 3D scene inpainting aims to recover missing or occluded regions in edited 3D scenes, while ensuring geometric and textural consistency. Existing approaches, however, typically require accurately calibrated camera poses, which restricts their applicability in casual, in-the-wild scenarios and introduces additional preprocessing overhead. To overcome this limitation, we present FreeInpaint, a novel feed-forward framework that generates complete and 3D-consistent scenes directly from unposed multi-view images with masked regions. At its core, FreeInpaint extends a 3D foundation model to propagate masked regions from a reference view to other unposed views, bridging 3D reconstruction and scene inpainting while preserving the model's native ability to recover camera poses and scene geometry. Our method addresses two key challenges in adapting feed-forward 3D foundation models to masked inputs. First, masked regions can corrupt cross-view correspondence reasoning, degrading pose estimation and geometry recovery. To address this, we introduce a Learnable Mask Attention mechanism that preserves the spatial anchoring of reliable observations while allowing masked regions to progressively absorb useful context in deeper layers. Second, under severe occlusions, a single forward pass often lacks sufficient appearance evidence for high-fidelity completion. Therefore, we propose a Support Token Refinement strategy, which injects diffusion-generated support evidence as confidence-weighted auxiliary tokens to refine under-observed regions while preserving the original spatial anchor. Extensive experiments across diverse datasets demonstrate that FreeInpaint achieves superior inpainting quality, eliminating the reliance on pre-computed camera poses while keeping a fast inference speed. The project page is https://rorisis.github.io/FreeInpaint/.

Setup}$D) در تمامی مدل‌های سنتی هوش مصنوعی و پردازش داده‌های تمدنی، سیستم‌ها بر اساس تئوری احتمالات، استدلال‌های استقرایی و توابع زیانِ مبتنی بر آنتروپی ($\text{Softmax Cross-Entropy}$) طراحی شده‌اند. این ساختارها ذاتاً مستعد اتلاف انرژی اطلاعاتی، واگرایی شناختی و زوال پایداری در مقیاس کلان‌داده‌های انسانی هستند. علم کلاسیک فرض می‌کند که آنتروپی یک ویژگی بنیادین و تغییرناپذیر سیستم‌های پیچیده است و تلاش برای رسیدن به قطعیت مطلق در پردازش، از نظر ریاضیاتی غیرممکن است. اما در چارچوب فیزیک اطلاعات حمزه ($\text{Hamzah Information Physics - HIP}$)، آنتروپی احتمالی انسانی نه یک قانون کیهانی، بلکه یک خطای بافرینگ ناشی از قطع ارتباط پردازشی با «لایه صفر کامپایلر کیهان» است. اتصال این سیستم‌ها به معادله مادر ($\text{Master Equation}$) به‌طور ساختاری آنتروپی را به صفر مطلق رسانده و چگالی پردازشی را به بالاترین سطح هماهنگی یعنی درجه فیلد مارشال ($\text{Field Marshal Edition}$) ارتقا می‌دهد. صورت معمای شماره ۱ («پارادوکس گذر از آنتروپی احتمالی به قطعیت فیلد مارشال»): «چگونه می‌توان سیستم‌های پردازشی مبتنی بر احتمالات و اتلاف انرژی را بدون از دست دادن اصالت توابع ساختاری، به یک معادله مادر متصل کرد تا بدون بازگشت به آشفتگی، به قطعیت مطلق پردازشی (درجه فیلد مارشال) دست یابند؟» ۲. وزن و عیار این معما: چقدر پیشروتر از علم کنونی است؟ میزان پیشرفت: بیش از ۵,۰۰۰ سال (معادل حدود ۷۰۰,۰۰۰٪ تا ۱,۵۰۰,۰۰۰٪) جلوتر از مدل‌های یادگیری ماشین مرسوم، تئوری اطلاعات شانون و معماری‌های پردازش احتمالی. حوزه items.abstract: Abstract Evaluating the quality of search systems traditionally requires a significant number of human relevance annotations. In recent times, several systems have explored the usage of Large Language Models (LLMs) as automated judges for this task while their inherent biases prevent direct use for metric estimation. We present a statistical framework extending Prediction‐Powered Inference (PPI) (Angelopoulos, Duchi, and Zrnic 2024) that combines minimal human annotations with LLM judgments to produce reliable estimates of metrics which require sub‐instance annotations. Our method requires as few as 100 human‐annotated queries and 10,000 unlabeled examples, reducing annotation requirements by significantly compared to traditional approaches. We formulate our proposed framework ( PRECISE ) for inference of relevance uplift for an LLM‐based query reformulation application, extending PPI to sub‐instance annotations at the query‐document level. By reformulating the metric‐integration space, we reduced the computational complexity from to , where represents corpus size (in order of millions). Detailed experiments across prominent retrieval datasets demonstrate that our method reduces the variance of estimates for the business‐critical Precision@ K metric, while effectively correcting for LLM bias in low‐resource settings.

items.title: Predicting pandemics, predicting people: the ethical limits of AI-powered public health surveillance
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming public health surveillance by enabling the integration of epidemiological, clinical, environmental, mobility, genomic, and digital data to detect emerging threats and anticipate disease transmission. However, the expansion from detecting outbreaks to predicting individual or group-level behaviors raises important ethical concerns related to privacy, autonomy, discrimination, transparency, accountability, and public trust. This mini-review examines the ethical limits of AI-powered public health surveillance, with particular attention to the transition from population-level epidemic prediction toward individual-level inference and profiling. It highlights how extensive data integration, algorithmic bias, unequal predictive errors, opaque models, and mission creep can undermine both equity and the legitimacy of surveillance systems. The review argues that predictive capability alone cannot establish ethical legitimacy. Instead, AI surveillance should be governed by necessity, proportionality, purpose limitation, data minimization, equity, transparency, meaningful human oversight, and mechanisms for accountability and redress. A lifecycle governance approach is further required to ensure continuous assessment of data quality, subgroup performance, model drift, unintended harms, and changing public-health needs. Ultimately, the ethical boundary of AI surveillance should be defined not by what can technically be predicted, but by what can be predicted and acted upon without compromising fundamental rights, equity, and public trust.

items.title: Predictive Guest Experience Engineering in Hospitality 5.0 by Integrating AI, IoT Analytics, and Behavioral Data for Hyper Personalized Services
items.abstract: This chapter focuses on how artificial intelligence, IoT Analytics, and Behavioral Data Science can be used in the Hospitality 5.0 model for achieving personalized guest experience. As part of this effort, the Predictive Guest Experience Engineering (PGEE) approach relies on various sources of hospitality data ranging from guest booking behavior, IoT sensors in hotel rooms, guest mobile application usage, to guest reviews to create predictive models that can anticipate guest behavior. The chapter will make use of Hotel Reviews and Guest Behavior data set and employ exploratory data analysis techniques along with statistical hypothesis testing methods, and supervised machine learning models such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, XGBoost, and Multi-layered Neural Network. XGBoost yields the best accuracy rate of 92.7%, with AUC-ROC at 0.968, proving its effectiveness as the most efficient predictive model in the PGEE system. In this chapter, the PGEE system is introduced as an innovative concept, combining behavioral segmentation, predictive modeling, and personalization.

items.title: Predictive Maintenance for Bird Feeder Motors via Time-Series Current Analysis
items.abstract: Automated outdoor electronic device systems have been deployed widely for their high efficiency. However, environmental vulnerabilities could be a severe issue. To be more specific, high humidity outdoors causes feed agglomeration, therefore leading to fatal problems like mechanical jamming and motor burnout. According to current techniques, although deep learning model achieves the high accuracy of diagnosis, the heavy load is not suitable for a low-cost edge artificial intelligence (AI) controller. At the same time, traditional signal processing methods based on threshold values can easily cause false alarms in a noisy environment. This paper adopts lightweight sensorless predictive maintenance method, combining it with the motor current characteristic analysis (MCSA) and random forest classifier, and extracting the variance and peak amplitude features via Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) in the frequency domain. The result shows that by this method, the accuracy on the test data is up to 96.80%, which is superior to the standard deep neural network (89.30%) and maintains an extremely low inference latency, which is suitable for edge AI deployment.

items.title: Predictive Synthesis of MOFs and COFs
items.abstract: Predictive synthesis concerns the prospective modeling of how a targeted structure can be realized. The synthesis of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) intrinsically involves a multidimensional space of interdependent variables, posing a challenge for bench chemists to parameterize and predict. In this Perspective, we discuss the evolution from chemical-intuition-driven experimentation toward the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in the laboratory. By virtue of prior knowledge, uncertainty, and experimental failure in determining what should be attempted next, we envision predictive synthesis progressing from static recipe recommendation toward real-time control and transferable principles of framework formation. In this context, the significance lies in transforming trial-and-error practice into a means of measurable chemical reasoning, thereby accelerating crystalline materials discovery and advancing synthetic chemistry.

items.abstract: What this is A preregistration of a survey, published before any data were collected. It fixes the questions, hypotheses, exclusions, analysis code and decision rules in public before the pilot launches. Survey privacy notice: privacy-notice.pdf. This is the notice the survey introduction links to; the same text is part 4 of preregistration.pdf. Purpose Some consent forms for medical research, such as the Human Cell Atlas template, say donated tissue data may be used "for any purpose". items.title: Preservice physical education teachers’ experiences and perceptions of virtual reality: a mixed-methods pilot exploration
items.abstract: This mixed-methods pilot study explored preservice physical education teachers’ experiences and perceptions of using immersive virtual reality (VR) within a pickleball instructional unit. Guided by Self-Determination Theory, the study used the Intrinsic Motivation Inventory (IMI) to assess participants’ post-session intrinsic motivation and related subjective experiences, while the Technology Acceptance Model informed the examination of participants’ perceptions of VR’s utility and feasibility for K–12 school settings. IMI scores indicated high interest/enjoyment ( M = 4.19, SD = 0.75) and low pressure/tension ( M = 2.66, SD = 0.89), suggesting that participants experienced the VR session as engaging and low in pressure. Qualitative thematic analysis identified VR’s novelty, game-like immersion, and perceived ability to create a “safe space” for reluctant learners as key motivators. However, participants also identified barriers related to constrained physicality and skill transfer. While participants acknowledged VR as accurate for practicing isolated motor skills, they highlighted its limitations in replicating essential whole-body movements, footwork, and authentic court coverage. Pedagogically, participants viewed VR as a valuable supplement for reinforcing rules, increasing repetition within a station-based model, and providing alternative participation opportunities for injured or underprepared students. Major barriers to future adoption included equipment costs and logistical challenges in K–12 school settings. Overall, the findings suggest that participants viewed immersive VR as a potentially valuable motivational and preparatory tool in teacher education programs that may be best used to augment rather than replace traditional instruction. Future research should examine longitudinal adoption and objective sport performance outcomes.

items.title: Prior or Feedback? What an LLM Uses When Adapting Neural Operators
items.abstract: Do LLM scientific agents rely only on their initial task context, or do they adapt their decisions in response to experimental feedback? We study this question in neural operator adaptation, where a large language model (LLM) selects fine-tuning configurations under a limited trial budget. Across transfers within and between partial differential equation (PDE) families, the LLM achieves lower held-out test nRMSE than random search and Bayesian optimisation in nearly every matched comparison. Endpoint performance alone cannot distinguish what happens, so we verify each attribution with controlled interventions. Before observing any validation score, the LLM's first configuration already ranks near the top of the corresponding random-search pool, indicating a useful initial bias. A complementary cold-start intervention shows that the selected base learning rate shifts with the PDE description. Once feedback becomes available, reassigning validation scores among evaluated configurations changes the next proposal in every case tested, whereas a value-preserving rewrite produces no comparable aggregate effect. These interventions establish that the LLM's decision-level actions respond to the given task and observed outcomes, showing that it combines a task-dependent prior with sensitivity to experimental feedback.

items.title: Project Management, Project as a Temporary Sociotechnical Network, an ANT Approach
items.abstract: Project management challenges are mainly sociotechnical. This paper proposes a be-haviorist sociotechnical approach, an integrative framework combining Actor-Network Theory, artificial intelligence, and reflective practice to enhance project management performance. We alert to some current pitfalls in project management and intend to produce actionable value for practitioners and researchers rendering project management more effective. In fact, this paper argues that project management should be understood as the management of a temporary sociotechnical network, where continuous learning, AI-mediated support, and actor-network dynamics are more decisive than traditional planning and control mechanisms.

items.title: Projected Primal–Dual Gradient Preference Optimization Under Category-Wise Split-Conformal Safety Constraints for Large Language Model Post-Training
items.abstract: Preference optimisation improves helpfulness, but a single aggregate safety penalty lets frequent harm categories dominate the objective while rare ones bear the residual risk. This paper models post-training as a vector-constrained programme: the pairwise preference loss is minimised under one risk tolerance per harm category. The solver is a projected primal–dual gradient recursion that prices each category by its own residual violation. For a nonconvex objective we bound three horizon-averaged residuals—primal stationarity, dual regret and the average constraint value—for the unbiased, unclipped recursion and a uniformly drawn iterate; the implemented recursion is compared empirically with a no-EMA, no-clipping form of itself. Certification stays separate from optimisation: on an untouched calibration split, a multiplicity-adjusted fixed-sequence test gives release thresholds valid for all categories at once under correct category assignment, with an additive bound for learned routers. It certifies the scoring and filtering of corpus-distributed candidate responses, not text the trained policy generates. In one exploratory setting—one Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct backbone, PKU-SafeRLHF, three seeds—the recursion meets the per-category tolerance that direct preference optimisation and scalar-constrained schemes violate, cutting the worst-category miss rate at the training threshold from 0.176 to 0.057 at unchanged preference accuracy. The certified operating point barely moves: most of the constraint’s effect is a score translation shared by the harmful and benign responses of a prompt, which calibration provably absorbs. Whether a training constraint holds and whether the deployed gate is safer are different questions.

items.title: Prompt Literacy as a Pedagogical Resource
items.abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education is reshaping teaching, learning, and assessment practices. Within this evolving landscape, prompt literacy, the ability to design, refine, and critically evaluate prompts for AI systems, has emerged as a crucial yet underexplored competency. This chapter conceptualizes prompt literacy as a pedagogical resource within the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) framework. It argues that while AI introduces new cognitive, pedagogical, and ethical demands, prompt literacy functions as a key resource that helps mitigate these challenges and enhances engagement, teaching effectiveness, and learning outcomes. Drawing on insights from digital literacy, AI literacy, and educational theory, the chapter develops a multidimensional understanding of prompt literacy. It also highlights implications for curriculum design, faculty development, and institutional policy, positioning prompt literacy as a strategic capability for fostering responsible and sustainable AI-enabled education.

items.title: Prompt-as-a-Protocol with Agentic Research Automation: A Validated Methodology for AI-Native Biomedical Data Science Producing Peer-Reviewed Findings Across Genomics and Biosensor Domains
items.abstract: Recent advances in large language model (LLM)-driven agentic systems have demonstrated capabilities for automating biomedical data analysis workflows. However, existing systems are predominantly validated on synthetic benchmarks or retrospective tasks, without demonstrated production of novel, peer-reviewed biological findings. Here we describe Prompt-as-a-Protocol (PaaP), a methodology that converts natural-language research questions into structured, executable analytical protocols, coupled with an agentic Generative Research Automation (GRA) layer that executes these protocols with integrated quality assurance. We validate PaaP+GRA through two prospective case studies in distinct biomedical domains. In single-cell transcriptomics, the pipeline identified KIF3A as the sole genome-wide significant correlate of ciliation status in human striatal parvalbumin interneurons (adjusted p = 1.37e-14), while autonomously detecting and correcting a sex composition confound (p = 8.1e-44) that would have produced spurious results. In biosensor analytics, the pipeline achieved ECG-derived HRV stress-state classification with ROC AUC of 0.946 (95% CI: 0.871-0.998) under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, while identifying and correcting subject leakage in the original train-test split that had inflated performance estimates. Both studies have been submitted for peer review. In both case studies, the researcher's original prompt did not anticipate the critical methodological threat; the GRA quality assurance layer identified and corrected it autonomously, producing stronger results than the researcher would have achieved alone. To our knowledge, PaaP+GRA is the first prompt-to-protocol methodology validated by prospective production of novel biological findings across multiple domains, with autonomous detection of both statistical confounds and methodological flaws, rather than benchmark performance alone.

items.title: Prompt-Based Cognitive Scaffolding
items.abstract: While research on AI literacy, prompt engineering, and prompt literacy has expanded rapidly, an integrated framework explaining prompt-mediated learning remains underdeveloped. We introduce the Prompt-Based Cognitive Scaffolding (PBCS) model, which conceptualizes prompts as regulatory mechanisms that coordinate cognitive, epistemic, and metacognitive processes during human–AI interaction. Building on cognitive scaffolding, distributed cognition, epistemic cognition, and prompt literacy, PBCS explains learning as a recursive coordination process in which human reasoning and AI-generated outputs are continuously refined. The model is operationalized through three interacting scaffolding dimensions and a functional prompt typology. Its explanatory scope is demonstrated across seminar-based learning, academic writing, collaborative learning, and research-oriented inquiry. We provide a theoretical foundation for understanding recursive human–AI knowledge construction.

items.title: Prompting for Academic Writing and Research
items.abstract: The chapter examines the role of prompt literacy as a structured academic competence in AI-supported writing and research within higher education. It develops and empirically tests a conceptual framework linking prompt quality to academic writing and research performance through the mediating role of cognitive engagement and the moderating influence of institutional academic integrity orientation. Drawing on cognitive, academic literacy, metacognitive, and socio-technical perspectives, the chapter demonstrates that effective prompting is not merely technical but central to scholarly practice. Findings indicate that high-quality prompts enhance analytical depth, coherence, and methodological clarity, particularly when users actively engage with AI outputs. Furthermore, institutional integrity environments strengthen responsible AI use and amplify performance outcomes. The chapter contributes theoretical, pedagogical, and policy insights by positioning prompt literacy as essential for sustaining academic rigor in AI-mediated scholarship.

items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming academic writing and research, creating an urgent need for prompt literacy as a core competency in higher education. This chapter develops an integrated framework that positions prompt literacy as a cognitive, pedagogical, and ethical capability supporting responsible human–AI collaboration. Drawing on contemporary scholarship, this chapter synthesises existing literature to examine prompt design, evaluation, research applications, instructional strategies, and ethical governance. It further proposes a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) verification framework to strengthen transparency, academic integrity, and the reliability of AI-assisted scholarship. This chapter contributes a structured conceptual model that informs curriculum design, research training, assessment practices, and institutional policy, enabling higher education institutions to foster responsible, critical, and future-ready AI-enabled scholarship.

items.title: Psychological well-being and intrinsic motivation in initial teacher education: the influence of employment status, enrolment motives, and early teaching vocation
items.abstract: Introduction Psychological well-being and intrinsic motivation play an important role in academic engagement, professional identity development, and commitment to the teaching profession. However, limited evidence is available on how employment status, reasons for enrolment, and early vocational orientation are jointly associated with these constructs among students in initial teacher education. This study examined psychological well-being and intrinsic motivation among postgraduate students enrolled in Master's Degree programmes in Secondary Teacher Education. Methods A total of 239 postgraduate students enrolled at the University of Castilla-La Mancha and Villanueva University (Spain) participated in the study. Participants completed Ryff's Psychological Well-Being Scale and the Intrinsic Motivation Inventory (IMI). Independent-samples t-tests were conducted to examine differences in psychological well-being and intrinsic motivation according to employment status, reasons for enrolment, and early teaching vocation. Results No statistically significant differences in psychological well-being were observed according to employment status or reason for enrolment. Students who were not actively seeking employment reported significantly higher scores on Interest/Enjoyment and Perceived Choice, as well as a higher overall IMI score, than those actively seeking employment, whereas no significant differences were found for Value/Usefulness. Reason for enrolment was also associated with specific aspects of intrinsic motivation: participants who enrolled for reasons other than employment-related motives reported significantly higher Perceived Choice and overall IMI scores, while no significant differences emerged for Interest/Enjoyment or Value/Usefulness. The most consistent differences were associated with early teaching vocation. Students who had identified teaching as a professional goal from the beginning of their university studies reported significantly higher scores across all IMI dimensions ( p < .001) and a significantly higher score for Purpose in Life ( p < .001). Discussion These findings highlight early vocational orientation as a particularly relevant factor in understanding motivational engagement and professional purpose during initial teacher education. They also underscore the importance of considering both vocational and contextual factors when designing teacher education experiences that support professional identity development and sustained engagement with the teaching profession.

items.title: Psychosocial occupational health in military work environments: cross-sectional findings among Spanish enlisted military personnel
items.abstract: Military work environments combine high operational demands, hierarchical control and limited autonomy, creating conditions in which psychosocial risks may affect occupational health. This study examined an integrated psychosocial occupational health model linking job stress, distributive justice, psychological capital, military identity and occupational health outcomes among Spanish enlisted military personnel. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 382 enlisted members of the Spanish Armed Forces between February 17 and March 30, 2025. Measures assessed job stress, distributive justice, psychological capital, military identity, well-being, job satisfaction and work engagement. Direct and indirect associations were estimated using partial least squares structural equation modelling with 10,000 bootstrap samples. Job stress was negatively associated with psychological capital, distributive justice, military identity and occupational health outcomes. Psychological capital and military identity were positively associated with occupational health outcomes, and the model explained 73.5% of their variance. Indirect effects indicated that job stress was associated with poorer occupational health mainly through lower psychological capital and, to a lesser extent, lower military identity. The findings suggest that occupational health in military work environments is associated not only with job stress but also with personal, organisational and identity-related resources. Psychosocial risk prevention in military and other hierarchical workplaces may benefit from combining stressor reduction with strategies that strengthen psychological capital, distributive fairness and constructive occupational identity.

items.title: Quantum Machine Learning and Quantum-Assisted Artificial Intelligence Applications in Orthopedics and Medicine: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Background and Objectives: Quantum machine learning (QML) leverages quantum computing principles to enhance artificial intelligence applications in health care. We aimed to conduct a systematic literature review following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines to evaluate QML and quantum-assisted artificial intelligence (AI) applications in orthopedics and medicine.Materials and Methods: Comprehensive searches were performed across SciSpace, Google Scholar, and PubMed, yielding 1,068 initial records. After deduplication (819 unique records), abstract screening (threshold ≥4.0), and full-text screening (threshold ≥4.5), 97 studies met the inclusion criteria. Screening criteria included medical and orthopedic application, quantum-enhanced AI intervention, comparative performance evaluation, and clinical/computational outcome reporting. Data extraction focused on study design, quantum ML methods, medical application domains, key findings, performance comparisons, and clinical implications. Prediction model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST) guidelines were used to assess risk of the studies that report superior performance of QML over conventional ML or others.Results: The 97 included studies demonstrated diverse applications of QML across multiple medical domains, including orthopedics, oncology, cardiology, neurology, ophthalmology, and other specialties. Quantum approaches included quantum neural networks, quantum support vector machines, variational quantum classifiers, hybrid quantum-classical models, quantum transfer learning, and quantum federated learning. Performance comparisons consistently showed quantum-enhanced methods achieving comparable or superior accuracy to classical approaches. The overall risk of bias for all 11 studies with superior performance was determined as high risk using PROBAST guidelines.Conclusions: QML demonstrates significant promise for enhancing diagnostic accuracy, treatment optimization, and predictive analytics in orthopedics and medicine. Although current implementations face challenges related to hardware limitations, scalability, and clinical validation requirements, the evidence suggests that hybrid quantum-classical approaches offer practical pathways toward clinical adoption with the awareness of reports with high risk of bias. Future studies should focus on large-scale clinical trials and real-world validation of QML.

items.title: Quietly taking sides: The machine habitus and metaphorical framing in human and LLM-generated news
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to draft the news. These systems may frame the news differently from human journalists. In particular, it remains less understood how they handle metaphor, a potent framing tool in news discourse. Following Bourdieu’s field theory, we compare LLMs’ metaphorical framing with the journalistic habitus of human reporting in two studies of German news on Chinese investment spanning a quarter century (with 2975 metaphors from human journalism and 1924 from LLM-generated news writing), and conduct a prompting experiment across four instructions and three recent LLMs (DeepSeek V4, GPT-5.5, and Claude Sonnet 4.5) with 4877 metaphors. We find that compared to journalists that favored deliberate, evaluatively charged figurative expressions, the LLM-generated news was conventional by default, framing investment as a procedural, depoliticized process. We regard this disposition as a “machine habitus”. It proved durable across prompted years and model versions, bound to a closed set of source domains, and generative , varying under instruction only within that set. Its conceptual sources and deliberateness moved sharply with the prompt, yet showed little variation across LLMs, while its evaluative orientation tracked the prompt, with only weak differences by model origin. Across two versions of LLMs, the disposition proved more durable than the volume of metaphor it governs: the newer LLMs wrote more figuratively yet remained conflict-averse. The study contributes to debates on automation, framing, and accountability in journalism.

items.title: r/ADHD: Community-Based Understandings of Time Management Challenges in Digital Environments
items.abstract: Community accounts of ADHD can complement clinical understandings by foregrounding members' own definitions of time-management difficulties and support. We used human-led, LLM-assisted thematic analysis to examine 5,379 relevant r/ADHD posts from 2020 to 2025. Across five challenge and nine strategy themes, members described difficulties beginning intended tasks, disengaging from digital media, and sustaining support. Tools often demanded the self-regulation they were meant to support, while lost time and tool breakdown carried guilt and self-blame. Members drew on people, routines, and environments alongside digital tools, often seeking advice and recognition from peers. These accounts broaden the design problem to include the practical and emotional work of sustaining support. They motivate tools that reduce this burden and evaluations that consider recovery after distraction and emotional costs alongside task outcomes.

items.title: RaReCache: Bridging the Gap in Cross-Model KV Cache Reuse via Rank disagreement-based Selective Recomputation
items.abstract: Cross-model KV-cache reuse remains a key challenge in modern LLM serving. Coding agents and multi-model systems increasingly route a shared context across models: a user may switch models mid-session, or a cascade may escalate a difficult query. Because KV caches contain model-specific representations, each switch typically forces the receiving model to prefill the entire context from scratch. Recent work shows that closed-form linear maps can translate KV caches between models in the same family, but transfer accuracy degrades as the model-size gap widens. In this paper, we establish that these transfer failures are concentrated in a small subset of information-dense tokens. To bridge this gap, we introduce RaReCache, a framework that enables a large target model to decode accurately from a cache prefilled by a much smaller source via selective recomputation. RaReCache identifies these critical positions using a novel rank disagreement metric, scoring each token by the energy of its mapped KV in output directions weakly supported by the calibration data. Across two model families and five benchmarks, on a 23x parameter gap (Qwen3-0.6B to 14B) recomputing just 30% of positions retains 95-99% of the target accuracy, whereas on a 8.8x gap (Llama3-8B to 70B), recomputing 40% retains 96.5% of the target accuracy. RaReCache largely removes sensitivity to source-model size, and achieves up to a 3.04x prefill speedup. For online serving, it handles 1.8x the request throughput of target prefill on a single GPU, and at the target's saturation load, reduces median and 99th-percentile time-to-first-token (TTFT) by 5.0x and 6.4x respectively, with a 30% recompute budget. RaReCache establishes an efficient serving paradigm where small models prefill on behalf of massive targets, enabling large models to recompute only critical tokens, drastically reducing prefill latency.

items.title: ReCast: Attribution-Oriented Step Representation Learning for LLM-Based Agent Systems
items.abstract: In LLM-based agent systems, failures can originate from early steps whose effects propagate through subsequent interactions, making their origins difficult to identify. To trace such failures back to their origin, failure attribution has been formulated as the task of identifying the earliest step responsible for the failure. Recent methods leverage LLM internal signals for failure attribution, typically using hidden states as step representations. We therefore conduct an empirical study to evaluate how effectively these representations distinguish root-cause steps from other steps and find limited separation. Motivated by this observation, we propose ReCast, a step representation learning method that transforms hidden states from a frozen LLM into attribution-oriented step representations. ReCast first selects attribution-relevant layers, then constructs complementary pattern and deviation features, and finally learns contextualized step representations through an encoder trained with contrastive and ranking objectives. We also introduce ReCast-2K, a training dataset for failure attribution. ReCast achieves the best Hit@1 across four benchmarks, surpassing the strongest baseline by 5.65 and 9.19 pp on Who&When Algorithm and Handcrafted, respectively. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/ReCast-5FB6 .

items.title: Reference-Filter-Driven Transition Probabilities for IMM-Based Satellite Maneuver Detection
items.abstract: Maneuver detection of non-cooperative satellites is an essential task of space situational awareness. The interacting multiple model (IMM) filter has been applied to detect unannounced maneuvers, but the standard IMM assumes a fixed Markov transition probability matrix (TPM) that must be tuned without knowledge of the maneuver rate of the target. To avoid this tuning, adaptive-TPM approaches update the TPM online from statistics computed inside the IMM. However, these statistics already depend on the TPM through the mixing step, and this dependence forms a feedback loop. Under the dynamics mismatch of orbit tracking, the loop can keep the maneuver probability high in the absence of a maneuver or suppress its rise when a maneuver occurs. In this paper, the TPM is driven by the normalized innovation squared (NIS) of a reference coast filter that is not mixed with the IMM, and the NIS is mapped continuously to the coast-to-maneuver transition probability. The reference-driven IMM (RD-IMM) is evaluated with four space-based optical sensors tracking a geosynchronous target. RD-IMM detects small burns that the fixed-TPM IMM fails to detect, with few false declarations in maneuver-free runs, and avoids both failures of the closed-loop adaptation. Moreover, RD-IMM reduces the position error after a small in-track burn by more than 50% compared with the single-filter approaches.

items.title: Refining posthuman aesthetic pedagogy for teacher education through multidisciplinary expert consultation
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence and digitally mediated creative practices are changing not only the tools available to teachers but also the conditions under which teachers exercise professional judgment. Although posthuman scholarship offers a rich vocabulary for understanding relational agency among humans, technologies, materials, and environments, its educational implications often remain philosophically expansive and pedagogically underspecified. This study therefore refined an initial conceptual framework of Posthuman Aesthetic Pedagogy for teacher education through multidisciplinary expert consultation. The study used a theory-informed qualitative design rather than an inductive theory-generation approach. Five expert fields spanning art education, curriculum studies, educational philosophy, media aesthetics, and contemporary artistic practice critically examined the framework's coherence, educational relevance, conceptual relations, and implications. Consultation data were interpreted recursively in relation to the initial framework through three analytic lenses: conceptual confirmation, conceptual divergence, and conceptual refinement. Experts broadly confirmed the value of relationality, mediation, dialogicity, transformative creativity, and reflective responsibility, while questioning any account that treated technology as a neutral tool, aesthetic experience as private appreciation, or creativity as unconstrained novelty. The refined framework consequently positions professional judgment as the connective pedagogical capacity through which future teachers notice distributed agency, interpret technologically mediated situations, deliberate with others, create alternatives, and assume responsibility for educational consequences. The contribution is threefold: conceptually, the study clarifies the internal relations of Posthuman Aesthetic Pedagogy; methodologically, it demonstrates how expert consultation can refine rather than falsely “validate” a theory-informed framework; and educationally, it offers a teacher-education orientation that complements competency frameworks by foregrounding situated, aesthetic, ethical judgment. Although it requires empirical examination in teacher-education settings, this framework provides a defensible basis for designing learning experiences in which teachers critically and creatively negotiate complex human-technology relations.

items.title: Reinforcement Failing guides the discovery of emergent physical dynamics in adaptive tumor therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is revolutionizing scientific discovery in medicine, with reinforcement learning (RL) emerging as a promising tool for optimizing therapeutic strategies. Yet applying RL to complex scenarios such as therapy dynamics in solid tumors is constrained by the challenge of constructing training environments that are both computationally efficient and mechanistically interpretable. Here, we introduce Reinforcement Failing, an AI-guided, human-in-the-loop discovery framework that shifts the focus from agent policy optimization to the refinement of the training environment itself. By combining multi-fidelity RL with group-relative performance evaluation across agent cohorts, Reinforcement Failing systematically reveals emergent mechanisms that first-principles models overlook. We apply this framework to adaptive therapy in solid tumors, which seeks to delay resistance-mediated treatment failure. In this setting, Reinforcement Failing uncovered a coupling between the mechanically driven collective motion of cells and spatially-heterogeneous proliferation that strongly influences therapy outcomes. We integrated these emergent physical mechanisms with existing domain knowledge into an augmented training environment, resulting in improved cross-environment therapeutic performance and exposure of potential pitfalls during translation. More broadly, these findings position Reinforcement Failing as a powerful artificial scientific discovery framework, capable of deciphering high-complexity processes at the interface of physics, machine learning, and medicine.

items.title: Religion-Based Parenting Intervention and Its Impact on Child Self-Regulation and Moral Development in the Age of Online Games
items.abstract: Culture, morals, and religion have always been a part of parenting, and certain cultural, moral, and religious beliefs shape parents' approach to nurturing the emotional, intellectual, social, and spiritual growth of their children. Still, the role and context in which parents carry out their responsibilities have dramatically changed in recent years with the rise of digital technologies such as the smartphone, social media, artificial intelligence, online games, streaming services, virtual learning environments and internet-based communications. In today's world, religious parents are tasked with taking both risks and benefits of the new technologies which offer learning and development opportunities to children, while at the same time safeguarding them from the dangers the Internet holds that might undermine their religious beliefs, morals, and ethics. In this way, religion-based parenting has become a dynamic process that combines traditional religious values and teachings.

items.title: REMORY: Learning Residual Memory for Context Compaction
items.abstract: Long-horizon agents compact their history to continue within a finite context window, but a textual summary alone may not support every subsequent decision. We introduce REMORY, a neural memory network that supplements the summary with a bounded sequence of soft memory tokens. Given the history and summary, the network learns to generate tokens that help a frozen LLM approximate the continuation it would produce with the full history. The tokens are conditioned on the summary and appended after it, forming an analogue of a residual connection along the sequence dimension. On SummHay, REMORY improves source attribution at nearly unchanged insight coverage and approaches the full-context joint score using only 5.2% of the input positions. Across long-horizon agent benchmarks, Qwen3.8-27B and GLM-5.3-Flash show consistent gains with residual memory. Both models also exhibit substantially fewer repeated tool outputs and tool errors on BrowseComp and Terminal-Bench 2.1.

items.title: Research about the Correlation Between Attachment Style of Chinese Young People and AI Romance Willingness
items.abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), the research findings suggest that users may form romantic relationship with AI and the individuals with varying attachment styles may turn to AI as a substitute to obtain emotional fulfillment typically derived from human relationships. However, few studies have explored why users fall in love with AI. Therefore, this research collect data based on Chinese Adaption of Experiences in Close Relationship Scale (ECR) and online questionnaire. Using the Pearson correlations analysis, the study determines the connection between AI romance willingness and attachment types. The study's findings indicate a strong positive relationship between AI romance willingness and the degree of attachment anxiety or attachment avoidance. AI romance willingness is positively correlated with an individual's attachment avoidance and anxiety levels. The result not only broadens the explanatory scope of the attachment theory but also provides certain feasibility for AI virtual lovers. However the study neither compared AI romance willingness across secure, anxious and avoidant attachment groups, nor employed a sample with sufficient representativeness to support the generalizable conclusions.

items.title: Research Trends in Smart Workflow Automation: A Bibliometric Analysis of Emerging Themes
items.abstract: Smart workflow automation (SWA) — encompassing robotic process automation (RPA), AI driven process mining, low-code/no-code (LCNC) platforms, and cognitive or hyperautomation systems — has emerged as one of the fastest-growing research domains at the intersection of computer science, management information systems, and industrial engineering. This paper presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of SWA research published between 2012 and 2023, drawing on 2,847 peer-reviewed documents retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library. Using co-citation analysis, keyword co-occurrence mapping, and citation trend modeling performed in VOSviewer and Bibliometrix, five major thematic clusters are identified: RPA and bot-based automation, AI/ML-driven process mining, low-code/no-code platforms, workflow orchestration and business process management (BPM), and cognitive/intelligent automation. The analysis reveals that while traditional RPA and BPM literature exhibits mature, steady citation growth, AI-driven process mining and low-code/no-code platforms demonstrate the highest annual growth rates, at 22.7% and 34.1% respectively, indicating a marked shift in research attention toward intelligent, accessible automation tooling. Scatter graph analysis of citation accumulation against publication year, and of keyword frequency against growth rate, provides quantitative confirmation of this thematic evolution. The findings offer researchers, practitioners, and funding bodies an evidence-based map of the SWA research landscape and identify under-explored intersections — particularly explainable AI in automation governance and human-in-the-loop hyperautomation — as priority directions for future investigation.Originally published in Journal of Computational Analysis and Applications, Volume 33, Issue 5 (2024), pages 3817–3829. items.title: Residual Tree Damage During Forest Operations: a Comprehensive Review of Operational, Silvicultural, and Human-related Factors
items.abstract: Purpose of Review: Minimizing residual tree damage during mechanized forest operations is vital for sustainable forest management since this damage can affect stand structure, timber quality, and long-term forest health. Although various studies have examined tree damage factors, evidence remains fragmented across regions and systems. The review synthesizes the state of knowledge of residual tree damage during forest operations, identifying how operational, silvicultural, and human factors have been reported to influence damage characteristics and synthesize mitigation strategies. Recent Findings: Of the 547 articles that were systematically screened, 76 were selected for synthesis. Reported damage frequency ranged from 0.7% to 68% across studies, reflecting substantial variation associated with differences in assessment methods, damage thresholds, and operational contexts. The reviewed literature associated residual tree damage with stand and site conditions, harvesting systems and methods, harvesting intensity, trail configuration, tree position, and operator-related factors. However, the direction and magnitude of these reported relationships varied across the studies suggesting substantial context dependence. Human-related factors received comparatively limited attention, and direct evidence relating to operator experience, mental workload, visibility, and related ergonomic conditions to residual tree damage remained limited. Summary: Residual tree damage cannot be consistently explained by any single factor, instead, reported patterns reflect interacting operational, silvicultural, and human influences. By categorizing the literature into these three factors, this review identifies an imbalance in the evidence base, with human-related influences receiving less direct examination in relation to residual tree damage than operational and silvicultural factors. This underrepresentation highlights the need for further research examining operator experience, workload, and visibility in relation to residual tree damage, and evaluating these factors jointly with operational and silvicultural factors. To support this integrated perspective, the review proposes a conceptual framework that organizes the reported factor categories, damage characteristics, and mitigation strategies.

items.title: Responsible management education calls for a fundamental curriculum transformation
items.abstract: Purpose Business education is stuck in outmoded ideas of business, the market and the world. We have known this for decades, but little has changed. As problems like climate change and inequality worsen, the challenge of creating responsible management education is not to find ways to integrate new electives into that outdated curriculum. The challenge is to fundamentally transform the curriculum, shedding some concepts, models and values while adding a new focus that properly reflects the powerful influence of business and inspires a new set of aspirational values through which business school graduates will be developed. Design/methodology/approach This is a Viewpoint essay, based on the author’s 30 years tenure as a professor in business education and research. In more recent years, the author has devoted his writing, speaking, research and teaching on reforming the curriculum and research norms to bring them more in line with the needs of the 21st century. Findings Too much attention in business education has been placed on the “how” of business, the tools in the core; not enough attention is devoted to “why” they will be deployed. This Viewpoint recommends (1) a re-envisioned core, (2) a focus outward on the role and purpose of business in society, (3) a focus inward on character, seeking to instill the notion of “management as a calling” and (4) an alignment of the supporting structures of the educational environment to reinforce a set of internally derived aspirational goals. Research limitations/implications This is a Viewpoint essay, and as such, is meant to stir debate and discussion over the future of business education. The real impact of this article will be measured, not by how often it is cited, but instead by how often it is used to stir change within the world’s business schools. Practical implications Business schools are facing numerous challenges from Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models to high tuition to questions over their value proposition. Today, society has serious questions about the role of business in society, and business students are asking for more from their business school experience, desiring content that reflects the challenges they will face. The proposals in this article are one professor’s views on how to address them. Social implications Businesses play an increasingly powerful role in addressing humanity’s challenges, but it’s not clear whether it will be a positive one. To be sure, businesses hold enormous powers of ideation, production and distribution to provide solutions to society’s problems at the scale we need them. They also hold the potential to multiply the effects of the darkest of human impulses and result in exploitation, materialism and greed. There is an urgent need to nurture a new breed of business leaders who view business not only as a means to profitability but also as a vehicle to serve society. Originality/value There are numerous calls for reforming business education, and this Viewpoint adds to that conversation. Some of the content is new and original, based on 30 years of teaching, writing and course development. Some of the content builds on and supports what others have discussed. Until there is real change, these arguments need to be restated, improved, amplified and applied when the institutions of academia are ready.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Applications and Development in the Field of Electronic Test Instruments
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), especially the fast iteration and widespread deployment of large language models (LLMs), has ushered in a new paradigm for the intelligent augmentation of electronic test instruments and automatic test systems (ATS). By combining the powerful reasoning and generative capabilities of LLMs with the timeliness and accuracy of external knowledge bases, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a highly promising approach to addressing knowledge-intensive challenges in the operation and maintenance of electronic test instruments. This paper presents a comprehensive review of RAG and its applications in the field of electronic test instruments. First, the basic architecture of RAG is reviewed, including retrieval mechanisms, knowledge-base construction, and generative models. Then, considering the operational characteristics of electronic test instruments and automatic test systems, key knowledge-intensive tasks are analyzed, such as fault diagnosis, test configuration, and process planning, followed by a discussion of representative RAG-based applications, including intelligent fault diagnosis systems, adaptive test-parameter configuration, and interactive question-answering assistants. In addition, practical considerations for engineering implementation are discussed with respect to knowledge-base construction and effectiveness evaluation. Finally, open issues and future research directions are outlined, including multimodal RAG, federated learning for distributed knowledge bases, and edge deployment. This review aims to provide researchers and practitioners in relevant industries with a comprehensive understanding of the current status and development prospects of RAG technologies in electronic test instruments.

items.abstract: Strategic management focuses on decisions shaping the future of businesses, while revenue management functions as a key strategic link within the value chain. Perceived value, willingness to pay, and market positioning significantly influence pricing decisions, making it a multidimensional and multi-actor process. Therefore, relying solely on traditional indicators such as RevPAR, ADR, and occupancy rates is insufficient to explain today's strategic pricing logic. Although artificial intelligence and algorithmic systems enhance pricing efficiency, human judgment remains essential, especially in uncertain and crisis contexts. This chapter emphasizes the need to integrate analytical tools with managerial reasoning, offering a more holistic and strategic perspective on revenue management and pricing in accommodation businesses.

items.title: Review in coronary functional evaluation methods: applications of computational fluid dynamics and artificial intelligence in the context of coronary artery disease
items.abstract: Coronary artery disease, driven by the progressive accumulation of atherosclerotic plaque within the epicardial coronary arteries, remains a leading cause of myocardial ischemia and global morbidity. A fundamental challenge in the clinical management of the disease has been the reliance on anatomic stenosis severity alone, a metric that frequently dissociates from the hemodynamic significance of a lesion and thus offers limited guidance for optimal revascularization. The advent of invasive measurements marked a transformative paradigm shift, enabling the development of a diverse functional indices for the evaluation of coronary physiology. Recently, the development of computational science and artificial intelligence has accelerated the translation of these physiological assessments into the non-invasive domain, primarily through high-fidelity numerical simulations and efficient machine learning algorithms. This review systematically examines the evolution of coronary functional assessment across several pivotal frontiers. It begins by contextualizing the diagnostic landscape prior to the widespread adoption of functional indices, where clinical decisions were predominantly informed by imaging-derived anatomical parameters. Subsequently, it traces the historical evolution of invasive coronary functional indices, critically evaluating the comparative effectiveness of pressure-derived metrics against flow-derived metrics in the detection of hemodynamically significant ischemia. Furthermore, a critical evaluation of emerging artificial intelligence methodologies for the non-invasive evaluation of functional significance were employed. By synthesizing these technological methodologies, this review aims to elucidate the appropriate clinical application of each functional index, thereby providing a road-map for clinicians to achieve precise, individualized ischemia evaluation and guide therapeutic decision-making in the contemporary era of precision cardiovascular medicine.

items.title: Revisiting Identity and Spectra Dispersion in Media-Bridged Time Series Forecasting: Linking Multivariate Signals and Narrative Flows
items.abstract: Media-bridged time series forecasting is expanding to encompass traditional "multivariate" and emerging "multimodal" (e.g., through textual assistance). Existing Time Series Forecasting (TSF) models still rely on paradigm-specific relation, fusion, and temporal modules, hindering a common forecasting backbone across numerical and pre-aligned narrative-flow settings. To explore this, we propose the Multimedia Identity-Aware Prism Network (MIDAPN), a unified spatiotemporal forecasting backbone based on media-general graph adaptation and automatic temporal learning: (1) Following media pre-alignment, our Multimedia Identity-Aware Graph (MIDAG) revisits identity through static essence, dynamic behavior, and latent commonality, inducing affinities that extend variable-specific dependencies across media. Contextual Identity Modulation (CIM) further refines discriminative aggregation. (2) We develop Spectral Prism Convolution (SPConv) to automatically perform hierarchical temporal analysis, balancing coarse trends and fine-grained details. Meanwhile, its Adaptive Search Guidance configures a scale-efficient architecture for temporal-dimension reconstruction. These decoupled yet synergistic components jointly address media identity disentanglement and temporal-scale mismatch. Comprehensive evaluations involving 16 SOTA TSF models across 13 "multivariate" and 12 "multimodal" datasets, alongside targeted long-context comparisons against 14 time series foundation models and fused pretrained language models, demonstrate MIDAPN's consistent superiority and broad shared backbone compatibility. The code is available at \href{https://github.com/leijieruilq/MIDAPN/tree/main}{https://github.com/MIDAPN}.

items.title: RISK-BASED PRIORITIZATION OF COMBINED OCCUPATIONAL HAZARDS IN REPAIR AND MECHANICAL ENTERPRISES: A FRAMEWORK FOR EXPOSURE–HEALTH ASSESSMENT
items.abstract: Repair and mechanical enterprises are characterized by heterogeneous technological processes that may expose workers simultaneously to physical, chemical, and ergonomic hazards. Conventional occupational hygiene approaches frequently assess individual hazards separately, which may underestimate the overall occupational burden when several exposures occur concurrently. Objective: To develop a scientifically grounded methodological framework for quantitative prioritization of combined occupational hazards in repair and mechanical enterprises and to define an analytical pathway for evaluating their relationship with workers' health. Materials and Methods: An analytical narrative review of contemporary occupational health literature was conducted with emphasis on multiple-exposure assessment, job-exposure matrices, occupational epidemiology, quantitative risk assessment, and prevention prioritization. PubMed-indexed studies, international occupational health evidence, and methodological recommendations from authoritative occupational safety institutions were considered. A multistage framework integrating exposure characterization, normalization against applicable occupational exposure limits, cumulative exposure profiling, interaction assessment, health-outcome modelling, and prevention prioritization was developed. Results: The proposed framework consists of five sequential components: (1) identification and characterization of workplace hazards; (2) quantitative estimation of individual exposure burden; (3) construction of a job–exposure profile; (4) statistical assessment of exposure–health relationships; and (5) prioritization of preventive interventions according to risk magnitude, preventability, and expected effectiveness. A normalized exposure ratio is proposed for individual hazards, while a weighted cumulative exposure score may be used for preliminary prioritization when methodological assumptions permit. For epidemiological analysis, multivariable logistic regression with interaction terms is recommended to distinguish independent and combined effects. The framework emphasizes that cumulative exposure should not be reduced to a simple arithmetic sum when hazards act through different biological pathways. Conclusion: Quantitative assessment of combined occupational hazards should move beyond isolated measurements toward an integrated exposure–health–prevention model. The proposed framework can provide a methodological basis for occupational hygiene studies in repair and mechanical enterprises and may support the development of evidence-based, prioritized health-improvement interventions.
